Fix Linear ticket COR-2206 in the entire-brain repo (you are in an isolated worktree of it). Follow the repo's CLAUDE.md / .entire/agent-guide.md workflow (Brain brief preflight etc.).

## Ticket: brain add: clone failure dumps git argv and duplicated raw git stderr (Low)

Repro: `entire brain add https://github.com/sandbox-audit/nonexistent-repo.git`

Observed:
```
clone: https://github.com/sandbox-audit/nonexistent-repo.git -> sandbox-audit_nonexistent-repo
clone_failed: git [--no-optional-locks -c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null/entire-brain-hooks-disabled clone --quiet -- https://github.com/sandbox-audit/nonexistent-repo.git sandbox-audit_nonexistent-repo]: exit status 128: remote: Repository not found.
fatal: repository 'https://github.com/sandbox-audit/nonexistent-repo.git/' not found
: remote: Repository not found.
fatal: repository 'https://github.com/sandbox-audit/nonexistent-repo.git/' not found
```
Problems: full git argv on the human surface, git stderr printed twice, a stray `: ` line.

Expected: one line — the URL and "repository not found (or no access)". The argv and raw stderr may live behind a verbose/debug surface. The no-egress gate message for this command is already good; don't touch it.

## Approach notes
- Likely in `internal/cli/add.go` (grep `clone_failed`). The duplication is probably the runner error already embedding stderr while the caller appends stderr again.
- Keep the fix scoped to the `add`/clone error path; do NOT refactor shared runner/error helpers that other commands use (a parallel agent is working on other error surfaces — avoid internal/factsync, connect, distill, privacy files).
- Match repo style: errors carry stable `snake_case:` codes; keep `clone_failed:` as the code. Classify common git failures (not found / no access) into plain words; fall back to a single de-duplicated summary line for other failures.
- Update or add a focused test pinning the new output (one test file max, no new frameworks).

## Workflow requirements
1. `git fetch origin main` and create your branch from `origin/main`: `git checkout -b cor-2206-add-clone-errors origin/main`.
2. Minimal change, repo idiom (comments explain WHY only).
3. Run `gofmt -l -s` on changed files (must be empty) and `go test ./internal/cli/ -run <focused>` plus one full `go test ./internal/cli/ -count=1` (takes ~7 min; it must pass).
4. Commit with explicit file names (never `git add -A`). End the commit message with:
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
5. Push the branch (a first push may be transiently rejected by the remote — retry once before investigating). Create the PR: `gh pr create --base main` with a cold-reader body (Why / What changed / Validation), ending with:
🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
6. Do NOT touch Linear; the parent session handles it.

Report back: PR URL, 3-5 bullets on what changed, exact new error output (from a test or built binary), validation run, any risks or behavior changes beyond the ticket.

a relationship question.

committed-tree results as analysis of edits they do not contain.

Ask per-symbol commands before bulk streams. Never dump unfiltered whole-repo

inspection. State unresolved coverage limits in the answer.

Both sets of mandatory rules apply.
Brain answers recorded-context and historical questions; Graph answers structural
questions and entity-level revision comparisons.

They NEVER replace required neighbors or impact analysis.
Graph results NEVER replace required retrieval of prior decisions or attempts.

location; it NEVER exempts relationship questions from Graph or historical
questions from Brain. Small edits, follow-ups, read-only reconnaissance, specs,

an answered question in source is not verification.

a reproduction, or the most relevant build. If execution is unavailable, disclose
that limit and perform a bounded source check. Prefer precise queries and line ranges,
but never trade resolution for fewer turns.

Current source and executed tests establish present behavior. Historical memory

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. When in doubt, don't spawn.
